questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements defining an
‘out-worker’:
I.
A person to whom any articles or materials
are given out to be made up, cleaned, or
altered.
II. A person who carries out the work either in
his own home or in some other premises not
under the control of the principal employer.
III. A person who is considered contract labour
under all provisions of the Act.
Which of the above statements is/are correct
regarding the exclusion of ‘out-workers’ from the
definition of a workman?
questions.explanation_english:
I and II only
Under Section 2(1)(i), an out-worker is a person
given materials to process in premises not under
the control or management of the principal
employer. Out-workers are explicitly excluded
from the definition of a workman under the Act,
making statement III incorrect and ensuring the
scope remains restricted to workers controlled
directly or contractually on-site.
questions.explanation_hindi: आउट-वर्कर वह व्यक्ति है जो दी गई सामग्री पर अपने घर या नियोक्ता के नियंत्रण से बाहर के परिसर में काम करता है; स्रोत में इन्हीं विशेषताओं को मान्य माना गया है।

questions.question_english:
Does the Contract Labour (Regulation and
Abolition) Act, 1970 apply to a contractor who
engages only 15 workers in a Delhi establishment
(where the state threshold hasn’t been lowered
below 20)?
options_english:
Yes, the statutory Act automatically applies
to all manpower contractors regardless of
workforce size.

Yes, the Act applies provided that the

No, the Act applies to contractors employing

questions.question_hindi: प्रतिष्ठान के पंजीकरण की प्रक्रिया के इन चरणों पर विचार करें: I. पंजीकरण अधिकारी को निर्धारित प्रपत्र में आवेदन देना। II. निर्धारित शुल्क जमा करना। III. पंजीकरण अधिकारी से पंजीकरण प्रमाणपत्र प्राप्त करना। IV. राज्य सलाहकार बोर्ड की अनिवार्य मंजूरी लेना। धारा 7 के तहत कौन-से चरण आवश्यक हैं?
questions.question_english:
Consider the following steps involved in the
registration of an establishment:
I.
Submission of application in the prescribed
form to the Registering Officer.
II. Payment of prescribed fees.
III. Issuance of a certificate of registration by
the Registering Officer.
IV. Mandatory approval by the State Advisory
Board.
Which of the above steps are statutorily required
for registration under Section 7 of the Contract
Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970?
questions.explanation_english:
I, II and III
Section 7 details the registration process:
submitting an application in the prescribed form
to the Registering Officer, paying prescribed fees,
and receiving a registration certificate. Approval
by the State Advisory Board is not a step in
registering individual establishments, making
statements I, II, and III the correct sequence.

questions.question_english:
If an establishment carries out work of a seasonal
character, it shall not be deemed intermittent if
the work is performed for more than how many
days in a year?
questions.explanation_english:
60 days
Under Section 1(5)(b) of the Act, if an
establishment carries out work of a seasonal
character, such work shall not be deemed to
be of an intermittent nature if it is performed
for more than sixty days in a year. Exceeding
this period indicates regular seasonal activity,
making the establishment subject to statutory
contract labour provisions.
questions.explanation_hindi: धारा 1(5)(b) के अनुसार, एक वर्ष में 60 दिनों से अधिक किया गया मौसमी काम रुक-रुककर किया जाने वाला काम नहीं माना जाता।

questions.question_english:
Read the following conditions related to the
applicability of the Contract Labour (Regulation
and Abolition) Act, 1970 to an establishment:
I.
It employs 20 or more workmen as contract
labour on any day of the preceding 12
months.
II. It employs 10 or more workmen as contract
labour on any day of the preceding 12
months.
III. It applies to contractors who employ 20 or
more workmen on any day in the preceding
12 months.
IV. It applies unconditionally to all government
departments regardless of the number of
workers.
Which of the above statements represent the
correct applicability threshold under the Central
Act?
questions.explanation_english:
I and III only
Under Section 1(4), the Act applies to every
establishment in which twenty or more workmen
are employed or were employed on any day of the
preceding twelve months as contract labour, and
to every contractor who employs twenty or more
workmen. It does not apply automatically to all
government departments regardless of workforce
numbers.

questions.explanation_english:

questions.question_english:
Before
revoking
the
registration
of
an
establishment under Section 8 of the Contract
Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970,
what procedural safeguard must the registering
officer follow?
options_english:
Obtain prior written permission from the
jurisdictional High Court

Give the principal employer an opportunity
to be heard

Consult all deployed contract labourers
individually regarding revocation

Issue a formal public notice in at least two
leading national newspapers
questions.explanation_english:
Give the principal employer an opportunity
to be heard
Section 8 mandates that before revoking a
registration certificate, the Registering Officer
must give the Principal Employer a reasonable
opportunity of showing cause against the
proposed revocation. This statutory safeguard
ensures compliance with principles of natural
justice before taking administrative action.

to be heard

As per the Contract Labour (Regulation and
Abolition) Act, 1970, work performed in an
establishment is NOT deemed to be of an
intermittent nature if it was performed for more
than:
questions.explanation_english:
120 days in the preceding 12 months
According to Section 1(5)(a) of the Act, work
performed in an establishment shall not be
deemed to be of an intermittent nature if it was
performed for more than one hundred and twenty
days in the preceding twelve months. Exceeding

threshold
establishes
non-intermittent
status, bringing the establishment under the full
statutory purview of the Act.

questions.question_english:

performed in an establishment is of an
intermittent or casual nature, who has the
authority to decide this question?
options_english: The High Court of the respective State
questions.explanation_english:

Under Section 1(5) of the Contract Labour
(Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, if a
question arises whether any work performed in

Government. The government decides this
matter after consulting the relevant Advisory
Board, and its statutory decision remains final
and binding.

If a Principal Employer engages a contractor who

options_english:
The Principal Employer commits an offence

The Principal Employer enjoys complete

questions.question_english:
Consider the following welfare facilities mentioned
under the Contract Labour (Regulation and
Abolition) Act, 1970:
I.
Rest rooms
II. Canteens
III. First-aid facilities
IV. Supply of wholesome drinking water
Which of the above facilities must be provided
and maintained by the contractor?
questions.explanation_english:
I, II, III and IV
Chapter V (Sections 16 to 19) mandates that
the contractor must provide and maintain rest
rooms, canteens (where threshold is met), first-
aid facilities, wholesome drinking water, latrines,
urinals, and washing facilities for the health and
welfare of contract labourers.

key_facts: Correct option (English): I, II, III and IV

questions.question_english:
Under Section 17 of the Contract Labour

and

rooms or suitable alternative accommodation

in connection with the establishment’s work,
